extracted.intended_audience: members of Mystery Writers of America; mystery/crime writers, publishing professionals, and genre readers
extracted.subtask_description: Newsletter announcement of the 2025 Edgar Award winners that also states eligibility, the purpose of various Edgar and special awards, and high-level judging and conduct principles used by Mystery Writers of America.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility (publication/production year)
rubrics_metrics.description: Honoring the best in mystery fiction, nonfiction and television published or produced in 2024.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The 2025 Edgar Awards honor works published or produced in the prior calendar year (2024).

rubrics_metrics.name: Award categories (genre/format-specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards are presented across multiple categories including Best Novel, Best First Novel by an American author, Best Paperback Original, Best Fact Crime, Best Critical/Biographical, Best Short Story, Best Juvenile, Best Young Adult, Best Television Episode Teleplay, and other special awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions/nominations are judged within these discrete category buckets (examples and winners are listed throughout the newsletter).

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of the Edgar Awards
rubrics_metrics.description: The Edgar Awards are presented to authors of distinguished work in various categories; named after MWA’s patron saint Edgar Allan Poe.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: They recognize distinguished achievement across mystery fiction, nonfiction, and television formats and are the premier genre awards administered by Mystery Writers of America.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging selection for fairness and impartiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Mystery Writers of America would like to emphasize our commitment to diversity and fairness in the judging of the Edgar Awards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judges are selected from every region of the country, from every sub-category of the genre, and from every demographic to ensure fairness and impartiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volunteer judge responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Thank you, judges — a very grateful thank you to all of the Edgar Award judges, who volunteered many hours reading and ranking all of the nominated works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The awards rely on volunteer readers who invest substantial time to read and rank nominated works; this is the operational basis for selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grand Master Award criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: MWA’s Grand Master Award represents the pinnacle of achievement in mystery writing; established to acknowledge important contributions to this genre, as well as for a body of work that is both significant and of consistent high quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection favors sustained, career-spanning contributions to the mystery field — e.g., contributions as a writer, teacher, and role model for aspiring writers (as cited in the announcement about Laura Lippman).

rubrics_metrics.name: Raven Award criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The Raven Award recognizes outstanding achievement in the mystery field outside the realm of creative writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples of recognized contributions include bookstores and organizations that provide service to the mystery community (author events, curated selections, creating welcoming spaces, community-building activities), as illustrated by the Face in a Book bookstore citation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ellery Queen Award criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: The Ellery Queen Award was established to honor 'outstanding writing teams and outstanding people in the mystery-publishing industry.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients are people (or teams) whose work in the publishing industry — editors, publishers, editorial directors, etc. — has significantly supported or advanced mystery publishing (example: Peter Wolverton’s editorial/publishing roles).

rubrics_metrics.name: Robert L. Fish Memorial Award
rubrics_metrics.description: Robert L. Fish Memorial Award — Endowed by the family of Robert L. Fish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The newsletter lists short-story winners under this heading (the award is presented in association with short fiction; examples of winning/recognized stories are provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lilian Jackson Braun Memorial Award
rubrics_metrics.description: The Lilian Jackson Braun Memorial Award — Endowed by the estate of Lilian Jackson Braun.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The announcement lists winning titles under this memorial award heading; the estate endowment is noted as the source of the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Simon & Schuster Mary Higgins Clark Award (presented on behalf of Simon & Schuster)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Simon & Schuster Mary Higgins Clark Award — Presented on behalf of Simon & Schuster.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The newsletter lists the winner(s) for this category; the presentation/sponsorship by a publisher is a defining feature of the prize.

rubrics_metrics.name: G.P. Putnam’s Sons Sue Grafton Memorial Award (presented on behalf of G.P. Putnam’s Sons)
rubrics_metrics.description: The G.P. Putnam’s Sons Sue Grafton Memorial Award — Presented on behalf of G.P. Putnam’s Sons.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Winners for the memorial award are listed; the sponsorship/presentation by G.P. Putnam’s Sons is noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special awards naming and purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Various named/special awards (Grand Master, Raven, Ellery Queen, memorial awards) recognize accomplishments that may differ from category awards for single works.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These awards may honor lifetime achievement, industry service, non-creative contributions to the field, or other distinguished service; the newsletter provides brief purpose statements and examples for several of them.

rubrics_metrics.name: MWA diversity and anti-harassment policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Mystery Writers of America welcomes people from all backgrounds, regardless of religion, race, ethnicity, gender identity, sexual orientation, or disability. We do not tolerate discrimination or abuse of any kind, including any form of sexual harassment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Members and guests are required to comply with this policy when participating in any MWA‑sponsored events; the policy is positioned as organizational expectation and rule of conduct.
